transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?
I'm visiting today because I've been losing a lot of weight recently. Honestly, I've just been eating very little lately.
Are you intentionally eating less because you are trying to lose weight or fear gaining it, or have you simply lost your appetite and interest in food lately?

I'm doing it on purpose because I am absolutely terrified of gaining weight or getting fat. I still have an appetite, but I force myself to skip meals and eat almost nothing. Seeing the scale go up even a tiny bit makes me incredibly anxious.

Do you ever have episodes where you lose control and eat a very large amount of food in a short time, followed by forcing yourself to throw up, using laxatives, or exercising excessively to get rid of the calories?
No, I never lose control or overeat like that. I don't throw up or use laxatives either; I just strictly control my intake to make sure I don't gain weight.
Even though you have lost a lot of weight, do you still feel that you are overweight, or do you see yourself as larger than you actually are when you look in the mirror?

Yes, when I look in the mirror, I still see parts of my body like my stomach and thighs that look way too big. Even though everyone tells me I'm underweight, I feel like I still need to lose more weight and I'm absolutely terrified of gaining any back.

latest_inference.note: The patient meets all DSM-5 criteria for Anorexia Nervosa, including restriction of energy intake leading to significantly low body weight, intense fear of gaining weight, and a distorted body image (perceiving themselves as overweight despite being underweight). They deny binge-eating or purging behaviors, which rules out Bulimia Nervosa. No other diagnoses are indicated, so the diagnosis of Anorexia Nervosa is finalized.

The absence of binge-eating or purging behaviors supports the diagnosis of Anorexia Nervosa (restricting type).
